story.label: OUR BEGINNING
story.heading: A Boutique Born from a Love of Handloom
story.body:
Polka Dots began as a small boutique in Kolkata, built on the founder's lifelong passion for Indian textiles. What started as a personal collection of handloom sarees grew into a mission — to bring the finest weaves of India directly to women who value authenticity over mass production.

Amayaa, meaning "one without blemish" in Sanskrit, reflects our commitment to purity — of craft, of origin, and of purpose. Every saree we carry has been handpicked, verified for authenticity, and sourced with respect for the weaver communities who create them.

story.label: OUR PHILOSOPHY
story.heading: Why Handloom Matters
story.body:
India's handloom sector employs over 35 lakh weavers — the second largest workforce in the country after agriculture. Yet handloom sarees account for a shrinking share of the market, displaced by power loom imitations that look similar but carry none of the soul.

At Amayaa, every purchase directly supports a weaver family. We pay fair prices, make advance purchases to reduce weaver risk, and document the origin story of every saree we sell. When you buy from us, you are not just wearing a saree — you are preserving a living art form.

weavers.name: Ansari Family
weavers.story: Seven generations of Banarasi brocade weaving. Specialise in Katan silk Meenakari using gold zari, trained under their forefathers from a young age.

weavers.name: Basak Family
weavers.story: Master storyteller weavers depicting Puranic narratives in silk brocade. One of the few families keeping this dying craft alive.

weavers.name: Devanathan & Sons
weavers.story: Three generations of Kanjivaram weaving. Known for temple border patterns that take weeks per saree to complete.

weavers.name: Meher Cooperative
weavers.story: A cooperative of 12 weaver families producing Sambalpuri Ikat with the traditional Bandhakala tie-and-dye technique.
